Core Frequency of Use: Intermittent daily sessions through standard client applications. 4. Detailed Functional Requirements Specification Functional requirements are cataloged with strict traceability codes using the syntax: FR-[Module ID]-[Sequence Number]. 4.1 Module 1: User Management & Authentication System (UMA) FR-UMA-001: The system shall authenticate user credentials against a hashed data store using PBKDF2 with a SHA-256 algorithm. FR-UMA-002: The system shall enforce JSON Web Token (JWT) session expirations exactly 15 minutes after initialization. FR-UMA-003: The system shall lock any user account automatically for 30 minutes following 5 consecutive failed login attempts within a 5-minute tracking window. 4.2 Module 2: Core Data Processing Engine (DPE) FR-DPE-001: The system shall validate inbound CSV/JSON data schema payloads against a predefined system structure prior to triggering execution pipelines. FR-DPE-002: The system shall reject any data submission payload that exceeds a file footprint size of 25 Megabytes (MB). FR-DPE-003: The system shall generate an isolated, chronological tracking log file inside the administrative directory for every data operation executed. 4.3 Module 3: Reporting & Telemetry Engine (RTE) FR-RTE-001: The system shall render real-time tabular analytics updates on the dashboard within 500 milliseconds of backend calculation completion. FR-RTE-002: The system shall provide secure PDF and spreadsheet data extraction options for all filtered query displays. 5. Render Success Receipt ──── │ │ Main Success Scenario (Flow of Events) The Standard End-User clicks the "Upload Batch Data File" link on the interface dashboard. The system surfaces a file selector dialog filtering strictly for approved data schemas (.csv, .json). The user selects their file bundle and clicks the "Execute Process" button. The system locks the interface view and transmits the raw data bundle via a secure multipart form payload. The system performs structural parsing checks to verify schema alignment and integrity rules. The system sanitizes the file contents against SQL injection variations. The system commits the clean data rows to persistent relational storage pools. The system unlocks the view interface and displays an execution complete banner with tracking hashes. Alternative & Exceptional Flows Flow 5a (Invalid Data Schema Exception): The system determines the inbound data bundle violates structure parameters or contains corrupted characters. The system halts processing loops immediately and rolls back any half-written transactions. The system generates an error log entry outlining the precise row error coordinate. The system flashes a warning message on the UI: "Process Aborted: Invalid Column Mapping at Line 42." Flow 6a (Payload Footprint Violation): The system detects the inbound payload package exceeds 25MB before running parsing code. The system drops the network connection immediately to preserve bandwidth. The system notifies the client view layer of the network file size constraint breach. 6. DataTransaction Record: Tracks transaction identifiers, execution time metrics, source metadata hashes, and owner references. SystemLog Target: Manages debug files, warning structures, error stack telemetry, and historical system checkpoints. 7. Rigorous Non-Functional Requirements (NFR) Non-functional parameters are mapped using the strict taxonomy code NFR-[Category]-[Sequence]. 7.1 Performance & Throughput Metrics (PER) NFR-PER-001 (Latency): The system API layer shall respond to search query actions within 200 milliseconds under an ordinary baseline volume of 500 concurrent connections. NFR-PER-002 (Throughput): The core framework engine shall ingest and parse a minimum of 5,000 transaction inputs per second without triggering memory leaks or process crashes. 7.2 Security, Confidentiality & Compliance (SEC) NFR-SEC-001 (At-Rest Encryption): The data subsystem shall encrypt all stored patient records and user identification profiles using the AES-256 standard. NFR-SEC-002 (In-Transit Encryption): The web server shall reject any inbound traffic connection that does not present a valid TLS 1.3 transport configuration layer. 7.3 High Availability & Fault Tolerance (AVA) NFR-AVA-001 (Uptime Metrics): The system platform shall maintain a continuous operational availability uptime target of 99.9% across every academic semester cycle. NFR-AVA-002 (Recovery Targets): The data tier configuration must yield a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) under 5 minutes and a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) under 30 minutes via automated failover triggers. 8. System Constraints & Boundary Conditions C-01 (Hardware Limits): The system prototype deployment build must operate cleanly within an environment restricted to 2 CPU Cores and 4 Gigabytes (GB) of RAM. C-02 (Browser Optimization): The client view engine must maintain compatibility with Google Chrome v120+, Mozilla Firefox v120+, and Safari v17+. It will explicitly drop optimization support for legacy Internet Explorer runtimes. C-03 (Regulatory Standards): The software platform must process user identity vectors in complete alignment with regional data privacy laws and university software safety frameworks. 9. Appendices & Formal Glossary 9.1 Technical Terms Dictionary PBKDF2: Password-Based Key Derivation Function 2. A secure cryptographic hashing algorithm that applies pseudo-random functions to keys repeatedly to neutralize brute-force attacks. JWT: JSON Web Token. A compact, URL-safe means of representing claims securely between two computing nodes. RBAC: Role-Based Access Control. An approach to restricting system access exclusively to authorized user categories.
